title: Wave unwind must distinguish a taken claim from an untaken one, and clear the worker row
action: Delta re-review of hpf-2 found two P2s introduced by its own fix, plus one carried over. (1) The Err(_) arm at prepare.rs:1483 unwinds unconditionally, but that Err is a union of two states: the claim STOOD and a reservation failed mid-loop (prepare.rs:941), or the claim door never claimed at all (prepare.rs:919, Delegate arms in handlers_write.rs:901-915). unclaim_cell is called with force=true, so in the second case against an exotic cell record it can bypass guard_claim_ownership and return ANOTHER live agent cell to open — writing through a claim conflict, which bee never does. Fix: make claim_and_reserve_for_dispatch report whether the claim was taken (an explicit flag or a distinguishable error variant) and unwind ONLY when it was; never force through an ownership guard the wave does not own. (2) Same arm: when no claim was taken, unclaim refuses, unwind_failed becomes Some, and the skip is labelled unwind_failed telling the operator to force-unclaim a healthy cell — a false alarm. After fix (1) this path must report the real reason with no unwind note. (3) Carried over from the original review: unwind_wave_claim (prepare.rs:1327-1350) releases reservations and unclaims but never removes the workers[] row registered at prepare.rs:1021-1025, so a prepare_failed unwind (prepare.rs:1536,1544) leaves a running worker row pointing at an open cell; run_worker_remove (state_group/workers.rs:204) exists and is unused. Remove the row in the unwind. Tests: an untaken claim leaves the cell untouched and reports its real reason with no unwind note; a taken-claim unwind releases claim, reservations AND the worker row.

truths: The wave never force-unclaims a cell whose claim it did not take
A benign untaken-claim skip carries no unwind_failed label
A real unwind clears claim, reservations and the worker row

trace.outcome: Fixed: dispatch wave never force-unclaims a claim it never took, and its unwind now clears the worker row too.

report.outcome: Fixed the two P2s from the hpf-2 delta review plus the carried-over item: claim_and_reserve_for_dispatch now returns Result<Result<(...), String>, (Err2, bool)> where the bool reports whether the claim door itself took the claim before an unproven-shape failure; dispatch wave only calls the force-unclaim unwind when claim_taken is true, and an untaken claim is reported as claim_refused with no unwind note. unwind_wave_claim now also removes the dp-r1 worker row via a new unregister_worker_for_cell helper.
deviations: a new pub(crate) unregister_worker_for_cell helper added in prepare.rs (worker_mutate is already re-exported crate-wide, no edit to workers.rs needed)
unwind_wave_claim made pub(crate) for direct test reachability
docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/dispatch.md updated per the dispatch context note, reserved before writing

checks.evidence: claim_and_reserve_for_dispatch now returns the claim-taken bool alongside its error, so the wave unwinds only a claim it actually took instead of inferring it from an error union
test dispatch_wave_never_force_unclaims_a_claim_it_never_took: a foreign-claimed exotic-shape cell stands untouched and lands in skipped as claim_refused
same test asserts no UNWIND FAILED note on the untaken path, so the operator is never told to force-unclaim a healthy cell
new unregister_worker_for_cell helper called from unwind_wave_claim; test unwind_wave_claim_clears_the_claim_reservations_and_the_worker_row covers claim, reservation and row together
